title: Automation Protocol for High-Efficiency and High-Quality Genomic DNA Extraction from Saccharomyces Cerevisiae
author: Nina Alperovich

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Zymolyase Stock
steps_raw.instruction: Prepare stock of Zymolyase 20T by dissolving to a concentration of 1 U/µL in 1x PBS.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Zymolyase Stock
steps_raw.instruction: Divide Zymolyase solution into 800 µL aliquots and store at -20 °C until use.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of 2-Mercaptoethanol Stock
steps_raw.instruction: Prepare 0.001 % stock of 2-Mercaptoethanol by diluting 1000-fold into 1x PBS.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of 2-Mercaptoethanol Stock
steps_raw.instruction: Store at 4 °C until use.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Digestion Master Mix
steps_raw.instruction: Add 22.72 mL 1x PBS

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Digestion Master Mix
steps_raw.instruction: Add one aliquot (800 µL) of Zymolyase Stock, 1 U/µL

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Digestion Master Mix
steps_raw.instruction: Add 160 µL 0.001 % 2-Mercaptoethanol

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Digestion Master Mix
steps_raw.instruction: Add 320 µL RNase A/T1 mix

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Digestion Master Mix
steps_raw.instruction: Prepare fresh before each use

steps_raw.title: Preparation of 4x Lysate Buffer
steps_raw.instruction: Add 30 mL Nuclease-Free Water.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of 4x Lysate Buffer
steps_raw.instruction: Add 60 mL 20% SDS

steps_raw.title: Preparation of 4x Lysate Buffer
steps_raw.instruction: Add 4 mL 0.5 mol/L EDTA.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of 4x Lysate Buffer
steps_raw.instruction: Add 6 mL 1 mol/L TRIS-HCL, pH 8.0

steps_raw.title: Preparation of 4x Lysate Buffer
steps_raw.instruction: Store at 4 °C until use.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Magnetic Beads Stock
steps_raw.instruction: Vortex Speed-Bead Magnetic beads to resuspend

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Magnetic Beads Stock
steps_raw.instruction: Divide Speed-Bead Magnetic beads into 1 mL aliquots, each in in a 1.7 mL Microcentrifuge Tube.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Magnetic Beads Stock
steps_raw.instruction: Place micro-centrifuge tubes containing magnetic beads solutions on a 12-Tube Magnetic Separation Rack until beads are drawn to the magnet and solutions are clear.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Magnetic Beads Stock
steps_raw.instruction: Remove supernatant.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Magnetic Beads Stock
steps_raw.instruction: Add 1 mL 1x TE Buffer to each micro-centrifuge tube containing beads, remove from magnetic stand, and mix by vortex.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Magnetic Beads Stock
steps_raw.instruction: Repeated steps 17-19 two additional times.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Magnetic Beads Stock
steps_raw.instruction: Store bead stock in the dark at 4 °C. Bring bead stock to room temperature and mix well by vortexing before use.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Magnetic Bead/PEG-NaCl Binding Buffer
steps_raw.instruction: Add 9 g PEG-8000 to a new 50 mL Conical Tube.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Magnetic Bead/PEG-NaCl Binding Buffer
steps_raw.instruction: Add 10 mL 5 mol/L Sodium Chloride.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Magnetic Bead/PEG-NaCl Binding Buffer
steps_raw.instruction: Add 500 µL 1 mol/L Tris-HCl, pH8.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Magnetic Bead/PEG-NaCl Binding Buffer
steps_raw.instruction: Add 500 µL 0.5 mol/L EDTA.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Magnetic Bead/PEG-NaCl Binding Buffer
steps_raw.instruction: Fill Conical Tube to the 40 mL mark with Nuclease-Free Water, then vortex to mix every 1-2 minutes until PEG goes into solution.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Magnetic Bead/PEG-NaCl Binding Buffer
steps_raw.instruction: Add 27.5 µL Tween-20 and mix gently by inverting 4-6 times.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Magnetic Bead/PEG-NaCl Binding Buffer
steps_raw.instruction: Vortex Magnetic Beads Stock (from previous section) to mix thoroughly.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Magnetic Bead/PEG-NaCl Binding Buffer
steps_raw.instruction: Add Magnetic Bead Stock:

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Magnetic Bead/PEG-NaCl Binding Buffer
steps_raw.instruction: For extraction of gDNA from liquid culture, add 3 mL Magnetic Beads Stock to the 50 mL Conical Tube containing the PEG/NaCl solution.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Magnetic Bead/PEG-NaCl Binding Buffer
steps_raw.instruction: For extraction of gDNA from yeast colonies, add 1 mL Magnetic Beads Stock to the 50 mL Conical Tube containing the PEG/NaCl solution.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Magnetic Bead/PEG-NaCl Binding Buffer
steps_raw.instruction: Fill Conical Tube to the 50 mL mark with Nuclease-Free Water, and gently mix until solution is a uniform brown color.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of Magnetic Bead/PEG-NaCl Binding Buffer
steps_raw.instruction: Wrap in foil (or place in dark container) and store at 4 °C, mix well by vortexing before use.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of yeast liquid culture for extraction
steps_raw.instruction: Aliquot 1.5 mL (OD600=1) in 1-3 columns of 96-well Spin Plate using automated multichannel pipettes.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of yeast liquid culture for extraction
steps_raw.instruction: Centrifuge at 3700 g for 10 min at 10 °C.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of yeast liquid culture for extraction
steps_raw.instruction: Remove supernatant from each well using automated liquid handler.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of yeast liquid culture for extraction
steps_raw.instruction: Use modified labware definition or other constraints on automated pipetting to set a minimum distance of 2.5 mm between the bottom of each well and the tip of each pipette.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of yeast liquid culture for extraction
steps_raw.instruction: The resulting volume of the remaining cell pellet and residual liquid should be approximately 50 µL.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of yeast liquid culture for extraction
steps_raw.instruction: Seal Spin Plate using Aluminum Foil Lid and Rubber Roller.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of yeast liquid culture for extraction
steps_raw.instruction: Store at -20 °C.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of yeast liquid culture for extraction
steps_raw.instruction: Defrost at 4 °C for 30-60 minutes before continuing with extraction.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of yeast colonies for extraction
steps_raw.instruction: Pick up colonies from agar plate and resuspend each in 50 μL of PBS in 1-3 columns of 96-well Spin Plate.

steps_raw.title: Preparation of yeast colonies for extraction
steps_raw.instruction: Proceed with DNA extraction from resuspended colonies as described below.

Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Pipette 315 µL of Digestion Master Mix into each well containing a cell pellet or resuspended colony; mix 30 times by repeated aspiration and dispense.

Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Transfer 315 μL from each well containing resuspended cell sample to a well in a new Reaction Plate located on a thermal-regulated microplate shaker.

Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Incubate at 37 °C for 25 minutes while shaking at 400 rpm.

Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Pipette 100 µL of 4x Lysate Buffer to each well and mix 3 times by repeated aspiration and dispense.
Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Incubate at 75°C for 10 minutes.

Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Move the Reaction Plate to a microplate shaker at room temperature.

Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Pipette 200 µL Magnetic Bead/PEG-NaCl Binding Buffer into each well.

Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Mix Magnetic Bead/PEG-NaCl Binding Buffer well by repeated aspiration and dispense before each transfer.

Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting After dispensing beads into each well, mix beads with cell lysate with one aspiration and dispense.

Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting During this step, the ratio of Magnetic Bead/PEG-NaCl Binding Buffer to the lysed sample volume is 0.48 (200 µL : 415 µL). Consequently, because of the relatively low PEG concentration in the mixture, only high molecular weight chromosomal DNA will bind to the beads.

Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Incubate at room temperature for 7 minutes while shaking at 300 rpm.

Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Move the Reaction Plate to a 96-well magnet base to pull the magnetic beads out of suspension
Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Wait for 5 minutes.

Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Remove and discard supernatant from each sample (approximately 615 μL).
Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Add 600 µL 80 % Ethanol to each well.
Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Wait for 1 minute.
Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Remove and discard the ethanol supernatant.
Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Add 300 µL 80 % Ethanol to each well.
Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Wait for 1 minute.
Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Remove and discard the ethanol supernatant.

Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting After removing most of the supernatant with large-volume tips, use smaller-volume tips (e.g., 50 µL) to remove any residual supernatant from the bottom of each well.

Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Allow magnetic bead pellets to dry for 5 minutes at room temperature.

Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Move the Reaction Plate from magnet base to an automated thermal-regulated microplate shaker with temperature set to 60 °C.

Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Add 100 µL Nuclease-Free Water to each well (note: can also use EB)

Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Resuspend beads by repeated aspiration and dispense (12 times).

Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Incubate at 60 °C for 10 s while shaking at 1000 rpm.

Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Incubate at 60 °C for 7 minutes while shaking at 400 rpm.
Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Move the Reaction Plate back to the magnet base.
Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Wait for 5 minutes.

Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Transfer the supernatant from each well to a new, clean well in the same plate (still on the magnet base).
Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Wait for 5 minutes.

Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Transfer the supernatant with extracted DNA from each well to a well in the Elution plate.

Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Cover the Elution plate containing the extracted DNA samples with a Universal Lid.

Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Optional (if protein contamination is problematic for down-stream application): Pipette 10 uL of Proteinase K solution to each well.

Yeast genomic DNA extraction. The following steps are implemented with an automated liquid handler, but can also be implemented with manual pipetting Optional (if Proteinase K was added in step 43): Incubate at 50°C for 25minutes.
